name: Herodias
overview: Herodias was a female figure in the New Testament known primarily as the wife of Philip, as noted in Matthew 14:3. She was the daughter of Herod and the half-sister to Philip, placing her within the Herodian family. Her identity is closely tied to her familial and marital connections.
namesAndTitles: Herodias is the only recorded name for this individual, and no specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to it in the biblical text. The name is simply recognized as her proper name as mentioned in Matthew 14:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Herodias was married to Philip, making her his wife according to Matthew 14:3. Additionally, she was the daughter of Herod and half-sister to Philip, establishing significant family ties within the Herodian dynasty.
scriptureSignificance: Herodias is significant in the biblical narrative as a member of the Herodian family, known for her marriage to Philip and her lineage as the daughter of Herod. Her connections highlight the complex familial relationships within the ruling family during the time of Jesus. These details provide context for understanding the political and social environment of the New Testament period.
